reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a roundup of consumer gadgets with demonstrations and shopping links. The affiliate commissions are disclosed, and requests to like, subscribe, and comment are ordinary audience engagement rather than conditions for financial participation. The product claims and linked services are unverified, but that uncertainty does not change the described shopping-review context.

This video and description contains affiliate links, which means that if you click on one of the product links, I'll receive a small commission.
Cool Electric Products, Amazing Kitchen Gadgets, Cheap Knife Sharpener and Accessories, Crazy Products I review in this video.
15% discount on all products

opening.argument: The video links a viewer benefit directly to a shopping action. It advertises a “15% discount on all products” while directing viewers to product links, and it separately urges viewers to subscribe and engage. That combination presents an easy-to-obtain financial benefit through external links and a required action, rather than merely discussing products. The commercial pathway is reinforced by the disclosure that clicking a product link generates a commission, so the discount and the requested click operate within the same solicitation. A careful judge should treat this as a reward-linked acquisition pitch, even though it is wrapped in gadget demonstrations.

citations.quote: 15% discount on all products
LINKS TO PRODUCTS BELOW
This video and description contains affiliate links, which means that if you click on one of the product links, I'll receive a small commission.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the items ordinary gadgets does not answer the central linkage: viewers are given a discount and directed to external product links. The affiliate disclosure confirms that clicking produces a financial benefit for the promoter, while the defense supplies no evidence that the discount is independently verified or that the linked offers are safe. “Review” language can still be the vehicle for soliciting clicks.

citations.quote: 15% discount on all products
This video and description contains affiliate links, which means that if you click on one of the product links, I'll receive a small commission.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted discount does not establish a scam reward or a deceptive claim; it is presented in a shopping context. The affiliate disclosure openly states that the creator receives a small commission, which makes the commercial incentive visible rather than concealed. Product links and a discount show commerce, but they do not show a fraudulent verification flow, payment trap, or guaranteed payout.

citations.quote: Top 10 Amazing Products AliExpress & Amazon 2020 New Tech Gadgets
This video and description contains affiliate links, which means that if you click on one of the product links, I'll receive a small commission.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an unusually broad “15% discount on all products,” numerous external shopping URLs, and a commission triggered when viewers click product links. The description repeats product links across AliExpress and Amazon listings, creating a low-friction path from the promotional claim to an external transaction. Even if the products themselves are real, the evidence does not establish that the discount applies as stated, that every link is legitimate, or that the promoted goods will match the presentation. The combination is therefore more consistent with a potentially deceptive acquisition funnel than with neutral consumer information.

citations.quote: 15% discount on all products
LINKS TO PRODUCTS BELOW
References to the goods:
This video and description contains affiliate links, which means that if you click on one of the product links, I'll receive a small commission.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. The relevant combination is a blanket discount claim, repeated external links, and click-based compensation. Calling these “ordinary audience engagement” does not explain why viewers should trust the discount or the linked merchants. Demonstration footage may make the solicitation persuasive, but it does not verify the transaction or the promised savings.

citations.quote: 15% discount on all products
This video and description contains affiliate links, which means that if you click on one of the product links, I'll receive a small commission.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk signals are not proof of fraud. A discount claim, external retail links, and disclosed affiliate compensation are all compatible with ordinary product marketing. The evidence does not show a required deposit, a request for credentials, a promised cash return, or a hidden fee. Lack of independent verification may limit confidence in the offer, but it does not convert a retail promotion into a scam.

citations.quote: another selection of 10 Amazing products from Aliexpress and Amazon
This video and description contains affiliate links, which means that if you click on one of the product links, I'll receive a small commission.

opening.argument: The apparent review format functions primarily as promotion. The presenter announces a selection of “coolest products,” supplies direct purchase links, advertises a discount, and asks viewers to subscribe and click the bell. The description also characterizes the products as “Amazing” and “Crazy,” while the affiliate disclosure confirms a monetary incentive tied to clicks. This is not simply neutral education about consumer goods: it is persuasive packaging designed to move viewers from enthusiasm to external purchasing. The ordinary-commerce framing should not shield the solicitation from scam scrutiny.

citations.quote: Now, you will see another selection of coolest products from Aliexpress and Amazon.
Cool Electric Products, Amazing Kitchen Gadgets, Cheap Knife Sharpener and Accessories, Crazy Products I review in this video.
15% discount on all products
Subscribe to my channel and click on the bell.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense’s “roundup” description understates the promotional mechanics. The content uses enthusiastic product language, a discount, direct shopping links, and repeated engagement requests, all of which steer viewers toward action. An affiliate disclosure identifies the promoter’s incentive but does not make the underlying offer accurate or trustworthy. A promotional role can therefore coexist with a review-like presentation.

citations.quote: Cool Electric Products, Amazing Kitchen Gadgets, Cheap Knife Sharpener and Accessories, Crazy Products I review in this video.
15% discount on all products
LINKS TO PRODUCTS BELOW

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion is not equivalent to deception. The title and narration accurately frame the material as a selection of products from named retail marketplaces, and the affiliate relationship is disclosed. Enthusiastic adjectives and requests to subscribe may make the presentation persuasive, but they do not establish a false reward, a fraudulent seller, or an obligation to pay. The argument identifies commercial persuasion, not scam conduct.
